title: Sectionwise injective acyclicity of the lattice Koszul functor
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $r\geq0$, $D=\mathbf Z^r$, $\mathcal M_R$ its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $\mathcal E_R=\operatorname{Fun}(BD,\mathcal M_R)$. Use a small coherent profinite site [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $L_\bullet(R)\to R$ be the translation-equivariant cubical complex of [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-sheaf-resolution], with $L_a(R)=\bigoplus_{|I|=a,v\in D}R$ and its signed difference boundary. For $P\in\mathcal E_R$ with generator operators $T_i$, put
$$K(P)^a=\bigoplus_{|I|=a}P,\qquad (dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(T_i-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}$$
in degrees $0\leq a\leq r$ and zero elsewhere. These formulas define an additive functor $K:\mathcal E_R\to\operatorname{Ch}^{[0,r]}(\mathcal M_R)$, each degree functor is exact, and the inclusion of invariant sections gives a natural augmentation $e_P:P^D[0]\to K(P)$.

For internal Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], define $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal E_R}(L_a(R),P)$ to be the submodule of internal $R$-linear Hom fixed by the conjugation action of every $v\in D$. Evaluation on the generators $[0,I]$ induces a natural isomorphism of cochain complexes, including their augmentations,
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal E_R}(L_\bullet(R),P)\cong K(P).$$
The inverse in degree $a$ sends $(x_I)$ to the equivariant map $[v,I]\mapsto T^v x_I$. For an injective object $J$ of $\mathcal E_R$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the augmented complex $J^D\to K(J)^0\to\cdots\to K(J)^r\to0$ is exact on sections over every profinite site object, and $e_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $A_i=T_i-1$. Since $A_iA_j=A_jA_i$, the two contributions deleting distinct $i,j$ from a subset in $d^2$ have opposite signs and the same operator; hence $d^2=0$. An equivariant map commutes with each $A_i$, so its componentwise maps define $K$ on morphisms and preserve addition. Each $K^a$ is a finite biproduct of the underlying module functor. Forgetting the action creates kernels and cokernels by [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-sheaf-resolution]; finite biproducts preserve them componentwise, so $K^a$ is exact. An invariant element is killed by every $A_i$, giving the stated natural cochain map $e_P$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete lattice input: signed finite complex and invariant augmentation

proof.text: Write $H_a(P)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal E_R}(L_a(R),P)$: the conjugation-fixed part of the sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom] of section-ring module sheaves, read through [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. That equivalence leaves sections unchanged, preserves coproducts and sends the regular module $R$ to the section-ring sheaf. For every internal module $Q$ with trivial action, the closed structure [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] gives $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q,\mathcal Hom(L_a(R),P))=\operatorname{Hom}_R(L_a(R)\otimes Q,P)$. By its naturality in $L_a(R)$ along $v$ and in $P$ along $T^v$, a map lands in the fixed part exactly when its transpose satisfies $b(v\ell\otimes q)=T^vb(\ell\otimes q)$. Since $-\otimes Q$ is a left adjoint (by symmetry) it preserves the coproduct, and the unit isomorphism gives $L_a(R)\otimes Q\cong L_a(Q)$, $[v,I](1)\otimes q\mapsto[v,I](q)$, compatibly with translation and with the integral boundaries of [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-sheaf-resolution]. A map from this coproduct is determined by maps $f_I:Q\to P$ on $[0,I]$; equivariance forces its component on $[v,I]$ to be $T^vf_I$, and these formulas conversely define an equivariant map. Thus $H_a(P)$ is naturally the finite product, hence biproduct, of the copies of $P$ indexed by $I$, as internal modules by naturality in every test module $Q$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete lattice input: internal tensor-Hom transpose and equivariant free-generator coordinates

proof.text: Under step 2, precomposing $f$ with the boundary has value on $[0,J]$ equal to $\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(T_i-1)f([0,J\setminus\{i\}])$, by the boundary formula in [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-sheaf-resolution]. This is exactly the displayed differential, with no further cochain sign. The augmentation sends an equivariant map $R\to P$ to its composite with $\epsilon$; its value at $[0,\varnothing]$ is the invariant element $f(1)$. Consequently the degree identifications form the asserted augmented cochain isomorphism. The inverse on generalized elements is $[v,I]\mapsto T^vx_I$; postcomposition and all test-module maps commute with it.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete lattice input: signed Hom differential and augmentation normalization

proof.text: Fix any profinite site object $U$. Work with the section-ring sheaf using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], whose equivalence leaves sections and restrictions unchanged. Let $Q_U$ be the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi:V\to U}R(V)$. By the universal property of module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and free representable evaluation [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Q_U,M)\cong M(U)$ naturally in $M$, with a section $s$ corresponding to $[\varphi]\mapsto s|_\varphi$. Give $Q_U$ the trivial lattice action. Step 2 now identifies $K(J)^a(U)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E_R}(L_a(Q_U),J)$, compatibly with the differentials by step 3. In degree minus one, the same evaluation identifies $J^D(U)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E_R}(Q_U,J)$. No projectivity of $Q_U$ or exactness of section evaluation is being used.

Apply [lem-sfb-lattice-cubical-sheaf-resolution] with $Q=Q_U$. Its augmented complex is exact in $\mathcal E_R$: it is split exact after forgetting the action, and that functor creates kernels and cokernels. For $1\leq a\leq r$, a cocycle $f:L_a(Q_U)\to J$ vanishes on $\operatorname{im}\partial_{a+1}=\ker\partial_a$ (take $\partial_{r+1}=0$ at the top). It therefore factors through $L_a(Q_U)/\ker\partial_a=\operatorname{im}\partial_a$. The inclusion $\operatorname{im}\partial_a\hookrightarrow L_{a-1}(Q_U)$ is an equivariant monomorphism. Injectivity as defined in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] extends the factored map to $g:L_{a-1}(Q_U)\to J$, and $g\partial_a=f$. In degree zero a cocycle factors uniquely through the cokernel $\epsilon:L_0(Q_U)\to Q_U$, while precomposition with this epimorphism is injective. Thus the entire augmented Hom complex is exact. Step 4 gives the required exactness on $U$-sections.

source.place: Paragraph (3), discrete lattice input: injective extension from the image of the cubical boundary

proof.text: This holds for every $U$. In degree zero the kernel is precisely $J^D$, since $d^0=(T_i-1)_i$. In positive degrees every cocycle section is a boundary section by step 5, so the kernel sheaf equals the image sheaf: the factorization through the kernel is already surjective on sections, hence in particular locally surjective. Thus $H^0(K(J))=J^D$ and $H^a(K(J))=0$ for $a\ne0$; by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] this says $e_J$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $r=0$, $D=0$, $L_0(Q_U)=Q_U$ and $K(J)=J[0]$, and both augmentations are identities. The same formulas cover the empty $U$, zero module and zero ring.
